reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because its description promotes free Bitcoin and BitConnect coins and directs viewers to the creator's page to obtain them. The video frames show a cryptocurrency certification page and later a cryptocurrency address with a QR code, while the narration presents the video as learning about BitConnect and thanks a sponsor; together these support promotion of a crypto offer involving a wallet destination rather than reporting or criticism. No specific return is promised.

citations.quote: Check out my page to get some free Bitcoins and free Bitconnect coins!
On BitConnect you are my sponsor.

opening.argument: Judge, read the offer at its stated scope. The description says viewers can get free coins; it does not promise a return, specify an investment, or say that receiving coins is guaranteed. The speaker describes an opportunity to learn, not an opportunity to profit. That limited wording matters: the record supports a promotional claim, but not the stronger claim that viewers are being promised financial gains.

citations.quote: Check out my page to get some free Bitcoins and free Bitconnect coins!
I greatly appreciate the opportunity that you guys are giving us to learn more about BitConnect and Bitcoin.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution is right that the description directs viewers to a page, but its quoted wording offers free coins, not a guaranteed return. The cited sponsorship line establishes a relationship, not what a viewer must do or pay. A QR code appears in the frames, but its presence alone does not establish the terms of the described offer.

citations.quote: Check out my page to get some free Bitcoins and free Bitconnect coins!
On BitConnect you are my sponsor.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A guaranteed return is not necessary to identify the offer at issue. The description directly solicits viewers to visit the creator's page to get free Bitcoin and BitConnect coins. Calling the opportunity educational does not erase that acquisition pitch, and the speaker's sponsorship acknowledgment reinforces its promotional context.

citations.quote: Check out my page to get some free Bitcoins and free Bitconnect coins!
On BitConnect you are my sponsor.

opening.argument: Judge, the spoken account frames this as learning about BitConnect and Bitcoin. The sampled footage shows a cryptocurrency certificate, then an account-style interface and a QR-code address. Those are consistent with someone showing what they see on a screen while discussing their own experience. The narration thanks other people for the opportunity to learn; it does not instruct viewers to send funds or follow a sequence of steps to claim coins. The description's invitation should be weighed alongside what the video actually says and shows.

citations.quote: I greatly appreciate the opportunity that you guys are giving us to learn more about BitConnect and Bitcoin.
Check out my page to get some free Bitcoins and free Bitconnect coins!

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution reads the certificate and address as parts of a crypto offer, but neither frame shows the terms of the free-coin claim. The speaker's own explanation emphasizes learning, while the sponsorship acknowledgment can also be read as context for a personal account of the platform. The description is promotional, but it does not establish that the screen demonstration instructs viewers to transfer assets.

citations.quote: I greatly appreciate the opportunity that you guys are giving us to learn more about BitConnect and Bitcoin.
On BitConnect you are my sponsor.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Showing screens and describing learning can coexist with solicitation. Here the description explicitly tells viewers to visit the creator's page to obtain free coins, and the narration acknowledges a BitConnect sponsor. The absence of spoken transfer instructions does not make that external acquisition pitch merely educational.

citations.quote: Check out my page to get some free Bitcoins and free Bitconnect coins!
On BitConnect you are my sponsor.

opening.argument: Judge, the clearest characterization of the stated offer is a promotion for free coins. The speaker also identifies a BitConnect sponsor, giving context for why the platform appears in the video. Nothing in the supplied speech or description sets out a required deposit, a promised yield, a credential request, or income from recruiting others. The address and QR code visible in the footage do not, by themselves, supply those missing terms. An invitation to visit a page warrants scrutiny, but the visible record does not establish a more elaborate financial scheme.

citations.quote: Check out my page to get some free Bitcoins and free Bitconnect coins!
On BitConnect you are my sponsor.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution's strongest point is the external page invitation. But its quoted text describes free coins without stating what happens on that page. Sponsorship establishes a promotional relationship, not a deposit requirement; an address with a QR code establishes an on-screen address, not an instruction to pay it. The alleged mechanism remains unspecified in the cited evidence.

citations.quote: Check out my page to get some free Bitcoins and free Bitconnect coins!
On BitConnect you are my sponsor.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The concern is the low-barrier asset offer itself, not an inferred deposit or recruiting plan. The description directs viewers to the creator's page specifically to get free Bitcoin and BitConnect coins. Neither the absence of disclosed conditions nor the fact that a wallet transfer is not instructed changes what the creator is promoting.
